subject: Animation
title: Color Coding Evil: Purple, Green, and Black
description: A micro-lesson that makes Color Coding Evil: Purple, Green, and Black usable.

hook.text: Disney villains are overwhelmingly colored in purples, greens, and blacks — colors that feel unnatural and toxic.

buildup.text: Maleficent uses purple and green. Ursula uses purple and black. Jafar uses black and red. The pattern is clear.

discovery.text: These colors trigger unease because they rarely appear in nature's safe zones — they signal poison and danger.

twist.text: Modern films are breaking this convention. Some recent villains use warm, inviting colors to subvert expectations.

climax.text: Villain color coding is a visual shortcut that has shaped how billions of people unconsciously read character design.

punchline.text: Purple and green mean danger because Disney trained your brain that way.

quiz.question: Why are purple and green commonly used for animated villains?
options: They are the cheapest colors to animate
These colors rarely appear in nature's safe zones and psychologically trigger associations with poison and danger
Walt Disney's personal favorite colors were purple and green
